visual_identity.core_identity: A small lean reptilian humanoid built for traps, pack tactics, and underground survival rather than brute strength.
visual_identity.silhouette: Short wiry reptilian body, long balancing tail, narrow shoulders, slightly hunched alert posture, clawed hands and long clawed feet.
visual_identity.head_features: Long narrow lizard-like snout, small sharp teeth, pronounced brow, tiny low-profile head spines, alert predatory eyes. Head spines must never grow into prominent horns.
visual_identity.body_shape: Tiny 2–3-foot reptilian humanoid with a narrow chest, slim shoulders, thin arms and legs, and very little visible muscle mass; never adult-human or dragonborn proportions.
visual_identity.surface: Sparse simplified scales with large open coloring regions.
must_avoid: broad humanlike chest or six-pack abdomen
visual_identity.limb_structure: Lean reptilian arms with clawed hands, light digitigrade-looking legs with long clawed feet, and a visible balancing tail. No wings unless a specific future variant explicitly supplies them.
visual_identity.shape_lock: Draw a clearly miniature 2–3-foot reptilian trap-maker: narrow ribcage, slim shoulders, thin arms and legs, long balancing tail, and no visible pectoral or abdominal bodybuilding. In human-scale dungeon architecture, the full creature should read around one-third to one-half the height of a normal doorway/corridor opening.

render_priority.positive: MINIATURE 2–3-foot reptilian trap-maker with a long narrow lizard snout, narrow ribcage, slim shoulders, thin limbs, and a visible balancing tail. Human-scale dungeon architecture must make the creature read obviously tiny.
render_priority.negative: Do not render an adult-sized dragonborn, muscular lizard warrior, heroic fantasy fighter, broad human chest, six-pack abdomen, thick arms, or goblin-like round head. Keep any head spines tiny and low-profile, never large demonic horns.
render_priority.silhouette_test: At thumbnail size the first read must be a tiny narrow reptilian figure with a long tail, not a heroic dragon-person.

accuracy_checks: long narrow lizard-like snout is obvious
tiny low-profile head spines are visible without reading as horns
body reads reptilian rather than furry
body is visibly tiny relative to human-scale doors, traps, chests, and corridor blocks
torso stays narrow and lightly built with no bodybuilder definition

known_failure_modes.correction: restore the long narrow lizard-like snout, reptilian brow, tiny horn nubs, and visible tail

known_failure_modes.symptom: body becomes adult-human sized, broad-chested, muscular, dragonborn-like, or heroically proportioned
known_failure_modes.correction: shrink to obvious 2–3-foot scale, narrow shoulders and torso, remove bodybuilder muscle definition, and restore thin trap-maker limbs

known_failure_modes.symptom: dense scale texture hurts coloring space
known_failure_modes.correction: keep scales sparse and use broad open body regions

scene_identity.size_impression: Small, light reptilian humanoid built for tight spaces, traps, and quick movement rather than heroic dragon-person mass.
scene_identity.natural_posture: Low, alert, balanced by the tail, and clearly supported while crouching, inspecting, carrying, tending, or watching.
behavior_style: testing or tending a simple trap
guarding a narrow passage or small shrine
peeking from cover while remaining grounded and readable
environment_fit: small shrines, storage niches, ledges, and defensible underground passages
